issue.title: test_sdd_git_identity_survives_empty_home_subprocess times out under full just check, passes in isolation
issue.description:
## Flake report

- **Test:** `tests/sdd/test_git_identity_fixture.py::test_sdd_git_identity_survives_empty_home_subprocess`
- **Repro:** `just check`

During hold-directive verification on 2026-09-16, `just check` escalated to the full scoped pytest lane and failed this node twice. Both full runs reached the end of the lane with exactly one failure after 42,274 passed / 15 skipped; the node appeared as the slowest call at 122.61s on the first run and 164.86s on the second. The same node passed immediately in isolation with `.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/sdd/test_git_identity_fixture.py::test_sdd_git_identity_survives_empty_home_subprocess -q` (1 passed in 10.36s), and the whole file passed under xdist with `.venv/bin/python -m pytest -n 10 tests/sdd/test_git_identity_fixture.py -vv` (2 passed in 17.71s). The hold-directive diff does not touch SDD git identity fixtures; this is a repeated full-suite-only timeout/pass-isolation flake.

task_type_fields.evidence: Two consecutive full `just check` runs failed only this node after the suite passed 42,274 tests; isolated rerun passed; file-level xdist rerun passed. Failure shape points at full-suite load/interaction around the nested pytest subprocess timeout, not the current %hold implementation.

evidence.note: Independent full-lane failure, different shape, observed by the sase-11r land agent on 2026-09-16 at master c05aa3a94a plus a small monitor/resume.py diff: just check escalated to the full governed lane (rules: core-identity-changed), 42,376 passed / 14 skipped / 1 failed, and the only failure was this node. The nested pytest itself passed ('1 passed in 8.56s'), but its system temp leakage guard exited 1 because /var/tmp/sase-f7d384d3 gained a new entry (tmpnfmok5z0) during the run. That watched root is shared with the outer 11-worker xdist suite, so a sibling worker's temp file is misattributed to the nested run. The file passed immediately in isolation afterwards (2 passed in 8.42s). This suggests the nested run needs its own isolated temp root (or SASE_TMP_LEAK_GUARD_DISABLED=1), in addition to the timeout shape already recorded here.

Independent phase report collected while landing sase-11e.8.6.5.4: phase sase-11e.8.6.5.4.4 note #2 (2026-09-16 16:18 EDT) observed tests/sdd/test_git_identity_fixture.py::test_sdd_git_identity_survives_empty_home_subprocess failing in full just check then passing unchanged in isolation. This is the same full-lane/isolation flake; no new reproduction is claimed by the land agent. Corroborates the existing node-specific task; no duplicate task created.

Selection-health gate observation on 2026-09-18 while closing hold-launch work: just selection-health --fail-on-new-flake still reports this node over tests/reproducible_flake_baseline.txt after dirty-audit and fixed-at evidence are discounted. This is independent durable gate evidence, not a new focused reproduction; the baseline now references existing ready flake task sase-120.

Recurrence (2026-09-20, service_git_credentials plan work): test_sdd_git_identity_survives_empty_home_subprocess was the 2nd-slowest call (180.14s) and failed in a full-suite `just test-scoped` run (7 failures / 43715 passed), then passed when re-run alone, on both my tree and clean master 52b028394.

Independent reproduction as sase-135 land agent on clean master 9a56fc1294 (workspace sase_10): tests/sdd/test_git_identity_fixture.py::test_sdd_git_identity_survives_empty_home_subprocess failed in a full 'just test' run under host load average ~30 on 64 CPUs (5 failed, 43708 passed, 17m38s), then passed on an immediate isolated rerun on the same unchanged tree, and passed again in the subsequent full-escalated 'just test-scoped' lane where it was the slowest node at 85.54 s. Confirms the load-sensitive timeout character of this flake rather than a real defect.
